summary: Turn needs evidence into feasible humanitarian response plans, logical frameworks, and review tools. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Humanitarian program design connects assessed needs to feasible response plans, intended results, and accountability. It is for program officers, technical leads, proposal writers, and partner managers who shape or review responses. Participants practise comparing response options, developing a Theory of Change and logical framework with indicators, and reviewing assumptions, risks, protection, and inclusion using Sphere Handbook and Core Humanitarian Standard references.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for people who make or support humanitarian response-design decisions, from needs prioritization through proposal review and partner planning.
modules: Sphere Handbook and CHS Design Checks
Theory of Change for Humanitarian Response
prerequisites: No prior humanitarian program-design experience is required. Familiarity with humanitarian response terminology is helpful but not essential. Coding is not required; exercises use program-design templates and a basic Excel worksheet.
